agree.reason: The calm tone, specific asks and the association's offer of a resident list and evening meetings make the letter hard to dismiss as a few loud people, but adding a fourth demand for a second-elevator study gives her an easy request to refuse and reopens a question she considers closed.

honest.reason: The facts are accurate and carefully hedged ("Keystone may be right"), but the fourth request for an independent second-elevator study is not one of the three things the association asked for, and "by mid-August" stretches a June-plus-six-to-eight-weeks timeline that could run to late August.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out "one day in every eight" and shows the June promise has already lapsed, but it never states that 74 of 112 households is two-thirds of the building, which is the figure that would answer the 'few loud people' view.

right_comparison.reason: The status quo is described fairly: the same six-to-eight-week promise has been repeated since June, and if nothing changes the same residents will be stranded with no repair date.

qualification.reason: The letter asks for a written reply with no deadline and no consequence if none comes, even though it will be posted and a TV reporter is lined up, so the reader has nothing dated to check against.

objections.reason: It anticipates the passing inspection by separating safety from reliability and accepts management's cost estimate, but it meets the 'only a few people' view only indirectly through the 74 signatures and never states the share of households.

fit.reason: It is a properly addressed open letter of about 430 words, readable both in a lobby and by a reporter, close to the requested length.
